reading.body:
Canva is the single largest vendor in this category, controlling three distinct tools, Adobe controls two, and Stability AI controls two, meaning roughly a third of the listed tools trace back to just three parent organizations despite appearing as separate products.

The geographic spread is wider than in most AI categories. US jurisdiction dominates with nine tools, but the Netherlands, UK, Australia, and France each host at least one vendor. That distribution matters for procurement and compliance decisions, because the same underlying capability, background removal or image generation, can arrive under different regulatory regimes depending on which product a buyer chooses.

Two tools, Blender AI Add-ons and Krita AI, run locally with no cloud dependency. That distinction is meaningful for power and infrastructure purposes: local processing shifts compute load and electricity draw to the user's hardware rather than a data center. The data does not specify the model sizes involved, the hardware requirements, or whether local inference is practical at production scale, so the infrastructure implications remain illustrative rather than quantified.

Commercial licensing and IP provenance are flagged repeatedly across the notes, for Adobe Firefly, DALL-E, Midjourney, Ideogram, and others, but the data records only that these considerations exist, not how each vendor addresses them. A reader evaluating legal risk would need to consult each vendor's current terms directly.
